card.title: Newton's second law
card.says: a nonzero net force accelerates an object in the **same direction** as $\sum \vec{F}$, with $a$ proportional to $\sum F$ and inversely proportional to mass $m$.
card.from: Isaac Newton's *Principia* (1687), linking how hard you push ($\sum \vec{F}$), how much inertia resists ($m$), and how fast velocity changes ($\vec{a}$).
card.useWhen: forces do not cancel and you need to find acceleration from forces, or an unknown force from a known acceleration; apply it separately along $x$ and $y$.
card.example: A $4\text{ kg}$ box on a smooth floor is pulled $20\text{ N}$ right and $8\text{ N}$ left → $\sum F = 20 - 8 = 12\text{ N}$ right, so $a = \dfrac{12}{4} = 3\text{ m/s}^2$ right.
card.analogy: Pushing an empty shopping cart versus a loaded one with the same push: the lighter cart picks up speed much faster.
